newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian postal, telephone workers call off strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian postal, telephone workers call off strike.

text.p: Indian postal and telephone workers called off a week-long strike on Tuesday after the government caved in and agreed to lift a ceiling on bonus payments, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.
Telecommunications Minister Beni Prasad Varma announced the cabinet decision on payments, reversing an austerity measure imposed by the federal government earlier this year.
The Indian news agency PTI quoted O.P. Gupta, head of the National Federation of Telecom Employees (NFTE), as saying that workers would return to work on Wednesday.
About one million postal and telephone workers went on strike last week in protest against the decision to impose a 3,500-rupee ($100) ceiling on annual pay bonuses.
Workers argued that a bonus ceiling for railway workers had already been lifted and that this set a precedent for other state sector employees.
Varma said the state telecommunications department would have to bear an additional financial burden of 1.2 billion rupees for bonus payments for 1995/96 (April-March).
Millions of letters piled up after six trade unions -- three of them representing postal unions -- went on strike.

The telecommunications department said earlier on Tuesday that striking telephone workers had stopped providing services such as repairs and billing in telephone exchanges. But most telephones were working because exchanges are automated.
The Indian Communications Ministry accused trade unions of failing to give sufficient notice before taking industrial action and declared the strike illegal on the day it began.
The unions had rejected promises from Varma and other cabinet ministers that the government would consider their demands favourably. They demanded that the cabinet take a decision on the issue.
A government statement said later on Tuesday that workers in government departments and organisations would be paid a productivity-linked bonus. ($1=35.6 rupees)
